output.name: Mirhan — The Gull Who Lost a Word (The Leeward Reach)
output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the wind carried Vel's messages down, and gulls carried them back. One grey gull from the cliffs was given a prayer for the Upper Sea. It was short, a mother's, for a son out on the water, and one word in the middle of it mattered most. Over the Leeward current, in a gust Tavo threw for his own sport, the gull dropped that word like a fish scale. It did not know it was gone until it reached the sky. Now it hangs below the Salt Ketch, which counts every sack and never once counted this, and it asks each boat it passes. Mesul, the ferry with no oars, takes the gull across and says nothing. Tessal's kettle sits full of sea-water on a hearth no one sits by, and each lantern shakes its head. Kael has tried to net the word and never caught one. On the cliffs they say that when the wind is wrong, the gull is near, so hold your tongue until it finds the word.
output.finding: Find Vesket, the Salt Ketch, and look about two-thirds of a hand-span (14°) straight south of it for the grey gull.
